title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Ops Playbook (SDKs, API Examples, Top Issues, Canonical Fixes)
author: Avery Chen
content:
Purpose and scope

This document defines standards, templates, operating procedures, and canonical fixes for Developer Experience documentation related to SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues we observe in the wild. Audience: SDK authors, technical writers, developer advocates, support engineers, and platform SREs.

1) Ownership and cadence
- Document owner: DevEx Content Team (Avery Chen)
- Maintainers: DevEx Docs squad + SDK owners per language (see "SDK OWNERS" below)
- Review cadence: Quarterly review + post-major-release (model/runtime)
- Change process: PRs to docs repo (git main->staging->prod pipeline). All PRs must include: list of changes, affected quickstarts, and at least one reviewer from the owning SDK team.

SDK OWNERS (examples)
- python-sdk: @samira (Samira Patel)
- js-sdk: @diego (Diego Martinez)
- go-sdk: @lena (Lena Okafor)
- docs-site infra: @infra-docs-sre

2) Document types & required frontmatter
Every published quickstart or SDK guide must begin with a standardized frontmatter block. Required fields (use YAML at top of md pages):

---
title: "Short descriptive title"
summary: "One-line summary of what the page covers"
type: quickstart | sdk-guide | api-example | troubleshooting
language: python | javascript | go | java | curl | none
owner_team: engineering | product | customer-success
owners: ["Name <email>"]
last_reviewed: YYYY-MM-DD
labels: [devex, quickstart, sdk]
---

Example frontmatter (JSON):
{"title":"Python quickstart: text generation","summary":"Show minimal SDK usage for text generation","type":"quickstart","language":"python","owner_team":"engineering","owners":["Avery Chen <avery@redwood.ai>"],"last_reviewed":"2026-03-27","labels":["devex","quickstart","python"]}

Template required sections (all doc types):
- Short intro (what, why, when to use)
- Prerequisites (accounts, SDK version, tokens, access)
- Quickstart (copy-paste runnable example)
- Full reference (API call details + params)
- Troubleshooting / common errors + canonical fixes
- Migration notes (if applicable)
- Links and related pages

3) SDK guide standards
Standards that SDK guides must follow:
- Supported languages: Python, JavaScript/Node, Go, Java, cURL examples included for every API surface.
- Minimum reproducible examples: 2 per guide (minimal and production ready).
- Dependency and version pinning: example Pipfile/requirements.txt or package.json with explicit versions.
- Auth examples: show both API key and short-lived token (OIDC) flows when applicable.
- Error handling: show canonical retry/backoff settings (exponential backoff with jitter).

Example Python quickstart snippet (minimal):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
resp = client.generate("Write a concise product one-liner for a developer platform")
print(resp.text)
```

Example JS quickstart snippet (streaming + function calling):
```javascript
import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-1.0-chat', messages: [{role:'user', content:'Summarize deployment steps'}] })
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.delta)
}
```

4) Quickstarts & templates (how to create and maintain)
- Standard quickstart topics: text-generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, file-upload + retrieval, fine-tuning / model-pinning, observability examples.
- Skeleton generator: docgen (internal). Usage: `docgen create quickstart --name "python-text-generation" --lang python --owner "Avery"` creates the MD and frontmatter.
- Naming convention: short-dash-case, include year only for archived examples. e.g., `python-text-generation-2026-03` for archived snapshots.

Skeleton checklist for every quickstart (must pass before publish):
1. Runs locally in a clean environment within 2 minutes.
2. Includes explicit SDK version and dependency pins.
3. CI smoke test added to docs repo (see CI section below).
4. Example output captured in fixtures/ with deterministic seeds when applicable.

5) API examples: patterns & constraints
- Always include both sync and streaming examples for generation APIs.
- Show function/tool calling patterns with explicit schema definitions and validation examples.
- Token guidance: include model token limits and recommended truncation policy per model. Example: redwood-1.0 has 32k token limit; recommend client-side prompt truncation at 31k with head+tail strategy.
- Rate limits: document per-account defaults and recommended client strategies. Example: hosted-api default rate limit = 120 requests/min by default; SDK should surface 429 with Retry-After header.

Example function-call snippet (JS):
```javascript
const res = await client.chat.create({
  model: 'redwood-1.0-chat',
  messages: [{role:'user',content:'Extract order id and total from this text'}],
  functions: [{name:'extract_order',schema:{type:'object',properties:{id:{type:'string'},total:{type:'number'}}}}]
})
```

6) Docs site operating procedures (builds, deploys, monitoring)
- Repo: git@github.com:redwood/devexp-docs.git, main->staging->prod pipeline.
- CI: GitHub Actions pipeline `docs-ci` runs on PRs: lint, spellcheck, build, smoke tests (headless Chromium docsite render).
- Build target times: full site build < 10 minutes on CI; staging preview available within 5 minutes of merging.
- Deployment steps (high level):
  1) Merge to staging -> automatic preview URL -> run smoke tests.
  2) Sign-off by doc owner + automated link-checker pass.
  3) Promote to prod via `./scripts/deploy-prod.sh` (requires 2 approvals).
- Rollout strategy: canary 10% of traffic (CDN edge) for 15 minutes, monitor for 5xx or asset errors, then 100% if stable.
- PagerDuty: service name `docs-site`; escalation policy: 5 min initial pager, 15 min follow-up to oncall-sre.
- SLOs: 99.9% availability for docs-site (internal SLA). Build success rate >= 98% for PR CI.

7) Smoke tests and automated checks (required)
- Static checks: markdownlint, link-checker, spellcheck (en_US), frontmatter validator.
- Runtime checks: render a subset of pages in headless browser, verify code blocks run for Python/JS quickstarts using test fixtures.
- Accessibility scan: axe run on sample pages every release.

8) Top support issues and canonical fixes (operational runbook)
We track the highest-impact recurring issues reported by Support and DevEx triage. For each: symptom, root cause, canonical fix, owners, and references.

Issue 1 — 401 / Invalid token errors
- Symptom: SDK calls return 401 with message "invalid_api_key" or "token_expired".
- Root cause: user is using provisioned API key incorrectly (typo, missing header), or short-lived token expired.
- Canonical fix: Verify header `Authorization: Bearer <KEY>`; ensure env var is set: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...`. For OIDC short tokens, ensure refresh flow: `client.refresh()` before request timeout.
- CLI debug: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ping`
- Owner: SDK-auth team, Support.

Issue 2 — CORS failures in browser-based samples
- Symptom: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` errors in browser console when using direct browser SDK.
- Root cause: customers embedding API key in client-side code or using server-only endpoints.
- Canonical fix: Use a short-lived token minted by your backend; proxy requests through your server. Reference quickstart: `browser-embedding-secure-2025`

Issue 3 — Outdated SDK version causing API mismatch
- Symptom: API returns unknown parameter or model name errors after platform rollout.
- Root cause: pinned SDK version does not include new API fields or model aliases.
- Canonical fix: Upgrade SDK per pinned migration guide. Example: `pip install --upgrade redwood-sdk==1.4.2` and run the migration test suite in `tests/migrations/`.

Issue 4 — Streaming disconnects and partial output
- Symptom: Streaming stops before EOS frequently for customers using unstable networks.
- Root cause: client-side timeout or aggressive reverse proxy chunking.
- Canonical fix: Increase client read timeout; set `stream_timeout_ms` to 90_000 in SDK config and set proxy to `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` passthrough. Example JS config: `const client = new Redwood({ apiKey, streamTimeoutMs: 90000 })`.

Issue 5 — Large payload / timeout when sending big file uploads
- Symptom: 504 Gateway Timeouts during large file upload or embedding creation.
- Root cause: client-side chunking not used, upstream gateway has low timeout.
- Canonical fix: Use multipart/chunked uploads (see file-upload quickstart). For CLI: `redwood-cli upload --file large-corpus.tar.gz --chunk-size 10MB`. Ensure gateway timeout >= 5 minutes for large batches.

Issue 6 — Embedding drift / incompatible vector dimension
- Symptom: Embedding vectors fail downstream similarity search (dimension mismatch).
- Root cause: Mismatch between model embedding dims and vector DB schema.
- Canonical fix: Confirm `model.embedding_dim` before index creation. Example: `redwood models describe redwood-embed-1.0` -> dims=1536. Recreate index with `dim=1536` or use on-the-fly transform.

Issue 7 — Rate limit (429) errors during load tests
- Symptom: Unexpected 429s for customers doing concurrent bulk calls.
- Root cause: not using batching or dedicated capacity when required.
- Canonical fix: Recommend batching/embeddings-bulk API or advise Dedicated capacity purchase. SDK suggestion: exponential backoff + jitter and use `client.batch()` where possible. Example backoff policy: initial=200ms, max=5s, attempts=6.

Issue 8 — Documentation build failures due to broken includes
- Symptom: CI docs build fails on staging due to `include` or relative path errors.
- Root cause: renaming files without updating includes or link-checker false negatives.
- Canonical fix: Run `docgen validate-includes` locally prior to PR; update references. Add failing page to `ci-skiplist` only with CTO approval.

9) Example canonical fix patch (auth header)
If support ticket shows token missing header, canonical fix PR should include: code snippet patch, updated quickstart, and regression test. Example patch (Python quickstart):
```diff
- client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
+ client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
```
Add CI test: `tests/quickstarts/test_python_auth_env.py` that asserts request succeeds with mocked server.

10) Release and rollback procedures for docs changes
- Emergency rollback: create a PR that reverts the last prod deployment commit and mark `docs-site` PD incident with "docs:rollback" tag.
- Hotfix process: branch from prod, minimum change, run smoke tests, merge with 2 approvers.

11) Metrics & dashboards (what to monitor)
- Build success rate (CI): target >= 98%
- Staging preview latency: median < 60s
- Prod page render errors (5xx): < 0.1%
- Broken links detected per week: < 5
- Number of support tickets referencing docs issues: decrease month-over-month after improvements

12) Onboarding checklist for new SDK writer
- Read this playbook and the "docs-writing-standards" page (linked).
- Run `docgen create` and push a sample quickstart.
- Pair with SDK owner to add one smoke test.
- Schedule first review within 2 weeks of first PR.

Appendix A — Useful CLI commands and snippets
- Create quickstart skeleton: `docgen create quickstart --name python-text-generation --lang python --owner "Avery"`
- Local preview: `make preview` (starts site on http://localhost:3000)
- Run link check: `make linkcheck`
- Run quickstart smoke tests: `pytest tests/quickstarts/ --run-slow`

Appendix B — Contact & escalation
- DevEx Docs Slack: #devex-docs
- PagerDuty service: docs-site (primary oncall: docs-sre)
- Support escalation: support->senior-support->sdk-owner path in playbook

Change log
- 2026-03-27: Initial published playbook (Avery Chen)
- 2026-04-02: Added streaming timeout canonical fix and updated build SLOs (Samira Patel)

End of document.
